sentences.text: The Daily Worker was a leftist newspaper published in Chicago and later in New York City.

Founded in 1924 by communists, socialists, union members, and other activists, the newspaper throughout its existence generally promoted the views of the Communist Party USA (CPUSA), although it also reflected a broader spectrum of left-wing opinion.
At its peak, the Daily Worker achieved a circulation of 35,000.

Contributors to its pages included Robert Minor and Fred Ellis (cartoonists), Lester Rodney (sports editor), David Karr, Richard Wright, John L. Spivak, Peter Fryer, Woody Guthrie, and Louis F. Budenz.
The newspaper ceased daily publication in 1958 and transitioned to weekly frequency under various names until 2010.
Since then, several online news and opinion outlets have claimed to be the Daily Workers legitimate successor.
Materials published by the Daily Worker prior to 1964 are in the public domain due to nonrenewal of their copyright status.
The Daily Worker originated as a weekly newspaper, the Ohio Socialist, published in Cleveland by the Socialist Party of Ohio from 1917 to November 1919.
The Ohio Party joined the nascent Communist Labor Party of America (CLP) at the 1919 Emergency National Convention.
The Ohio Socialist was renamed Toiler in November 1919.
The last Ohio Socialist issue was #94 November 19, 1919.
The Toiler continued this numbering sequence (although a typographical error caused its debut issue on November 26, 1919 to be #85 instead of #95).
In 1921, the volume 'IV' was added, perhaps indicating the publication's fourth year in print.
The final edition of the Toiler was Vol. IV #207 January 28, 1922.
The Worker continued the Toilers numbering during its run: Vol. IV #208 February 2, 1922 to Vol. VI #310 January 12, 1924.
The first Daily Worker edition was Vol. I #311.
In 1920, with the CLP going underground, Toiler served as the Party's "aboveground" newspaper, put out by "The Toiler Publishing Association".
It remained the paper of the CLP and its successors until February 1922.

In December 1921 the Workers Party of America was founded and the Toiler merged with the biweekly Workers Council of the Workers' Council of the United States to found a six-page weekly, The Worker, published out of Chicago.
On January 13, 1924, it was converted to daily frequency and relaunched as the Daily Worker, using $100,000 that had been raised from an assortment of Communist-led groups.
In 1927, the Daily Worker headquarters moved from Chicago to New York City.
Beginning in the popular front period of the 1930s, the Daily Worker broadened its coverage of the arts and entertainment.
In 1935, it added comic strips and a sports page.
With contributions from David Karr, the sports page was edited and often written by Lester Rodney.
The sports coverage combined enthusiasm for baseball with the usual Marxist social critique of capitalist society and bourgeois attitudes.
It advocated for the desegregation of professional sports.
The McCarthy era compelled many subscribers to switch to less notoriously "Red" newspapers, and circulation of the Daily Worker dropped below 10,000.
Finally, in January 1958, the paper stopped publication.
On the cover of its final issue on January 13, the editorial board said it had been overwhelmed by "the financial burden on a shrinking Left-Wing movement beset by internal difficulties."
Later that year, the Party introduced a weekend paper called The Worker, which ran till 1968.
A Tuesday edition called The Midweek Worker was added in 1961, and also operated through 1968.
In 1968, the publication was resumed as a New York daily paper, titled Daily World.
In 1986 it merged with the West Coast weekly paper, the People's World, forming the People's Daily World.
It lasted until 1991 when daily publication ended.
The new paper was cut back to weekly frequency and retitled People's Weekly World (later retitled People's World as to de-emphasize the weekly component).
Print publication of People's World ceased in 2010 in favor of an online edition.
, People's World claims that, "Peoplesworld.org is a daily news website of, for and by the 99% and the direct descendant of the Daily Worker."
Its publisher is Long View Publishing Company.
The online newspaper is a member of the International Labor Communications Association and is indexed in the Alternative Press Index.
Its staff members belong to the Newspaper Guild/CWA, AFL–CIO.
Another publication, both in print as The Worker and online as Daily Worker USA, states that it is "Continuing The Daily Worker, Founded in 1924."

The Worker is the Publication of the Central Committee of the Party of Communists USA, which itself claims to be continuing the legacy of the old CPUSA, and The Worker has been printed and distributed since at least 2020.

caveats.text: This article was chosen by subject (Socialism, communism and Marxism), not because Wikipedia marks it as a contentious topic. Wikipedia has no special sanctions area for this subject, so only Wikipedia-wide bans and sockpuppetry findings can count here. Topic bans do not apply.
